prompts: Mike finds the drawing Will made of the party — the one where the wizard looks a little too much like Mike. It's tucked in a book Will lent him. Neither of them mentions it, but the air changes.
Snowball dance, alternate ending. Will doesn't run to the bathroom this time. He asks Mike to dance, and to his own shock, the words actually come out.
It's the summer after Vecna. Will and Mike are the only two awake at 3 a.m. in the Byers' new house in California, sitting on the floor because neither can sleep.
Mike drives to Lenora to visit for spring break. Will meant to act normal. He does not act normal.
A thunderstorm knocks the power out during a campaign. Everyone else goes home. Will and Mike are left with a single candle and a conversation they've been avoiding for years.
Will overhears Mike on the phone with El, saying the words 'I don't think it was ever really about her.' He shouldn't have heard that. He can't un-hear it.
The painting. Will finally tells Mike the truth about who really commissioned it. Set it right after the van scene in season 4 — or wherever you want.
Post-canon: they're moving into a tiny apartment together 'as roommates.' There is one bed. There has always, somehow, been one bed.
Mike keeps the walkie-talkie under his pillow long after they should've outgrown it. One night, static — then Will's voice, calling him like it's 1983 again.
Will teaches Mike how to paint. Mike is terrible at it. Neither of them cares, because Will keeps having to lean in to fix Mike's grip on the brush.
Truth or dare with the party, but Max is merciless and she has known about both of them for years.
It's Will's birthday and Mike shows up with a gift that says, without saying, everything he's never had the courage to.
They fight. A real one, years in the making. Say something you can't take back — then figure out how they find their way back to each other.
The Upside Down took something from Will that only Mike ever noticed was missing. Post-recovery, Mike is determined to help him find it again.
College. Will and Mike end up at the same school by a coincidence that is absolutely not a coincidence, and share a dorm hallway.
A rainy road trip. One motel. Mike falls asleep on Will's shoulder in the car and Will doesn't dare move for two hundred miles.
El and Will have a quiet conversation about Mike. It goes gentler, and braver, than either of them expected.
Mike memorized the sound of Will's laugh sometime around 1984 and only just realized it. He's realizing a lot of things lately.
The party graduates high school. Everyone's talking about the future. Will can only think about one specific part of his.
Will draws Mike, in secret, for the hundredth time. This time Mike walks in before he can hide the sketchbook.
A slow dance in an empty gym while cleaning up after a school event nobody else stayed for.
Mike writes a letter he never intends to send. Will finds it. Take it from there.
Christmas at the Wheelers'. Mistletoe is involved, and Nancy is enjoying this far too much.
They're both grown now — late twenties — and reunite at a party reunion after years apart. Everything they never said is still sitting right there between them.
The Void. Will is pulled somewhere dark again, and the only anchor pulling him back is a voice he'd know anywhere.
Mike gets jealous of someone new in Will's life in California, and it forces him to admit — at least to himself — exactly what that jealousy means.
D&D made flesh: Will is the cleric, Mike is the paladin sworn to the party. When the healing runs out mid-quest, Mike is the one kneeling in the dirt refusing to let him go.
Will is a sorcerer who never asked for his magic, and Mike is the knight assigned to guard him from the people who want it. Neither of them is very good at keeping their distance.
A witch and his familiar. Will's spells have gone strange lately, and every single one of them keeps pointing at the boy who was supposed to just be a black cat on his windowsill.
Hogwarts AU. Mike is the Gryffindor who shouldn't be in the Hufflepuff common room at midnight, and Will is the one who keeps leaving the door unlocked anyway.
Mike is a pirate captain with a bad reputation and worse manners. Will is the thing tangled in his nets that is very much not a fish, and very much not letting go of his wrist.
Vampire AU. Will has been nineteen since 1986 and Mike has just recognized him across a crowded bar, forty years too late and not aged a day in his memory.
Ghost story: Mike buys a crumbling house in Hawkins and the boy who's been haunting it since the eighties knows things about him he never told anyone alive.
Angel and demon, both stationed in the same nothing town, both bad at their jobs, both filing reports that leave out the important parts about each other.
Rockstar Mike is playing the biggest show of his life and the tattoo artist he keeps flying across three states to see is standing in the wings again.
Two teachers, one staff room. Mike teaches English, Will teaches art, and the kids figured it out approximately a year before either of them did.
Will is a figure skater and Mike plays hockey and they share the same terrible 5 a.m. ice time. It starts as a turf war.
Summer job AU: Mike is stuck in the Scoops Ahoy sailor hat and Will is delivering for Surfer Boy Pizza. Both of them keep inventing reasons to be at the other's counter.
The Hawkins arcade, closing shift, 1985. Mike has one quarter left and Will is the only person who's ever beaten his high score.
Coffee shop, present day. Will has written the same wrong name on the cup for a month and Mike has stopped correcting him.
Regency AU: a painter of no particular fortune and the heir who keeps commissioning portraits he does not need.
Ancient Greece — a soldier and the oracle who keeps seeing the same ending and refuses to say it out loud.
1800s expedition, somewhere cold and unmapped. Two men, one tent, and a journal that stops being about the survey around week six.
Soulmate AU where the mark shows up the first time the other person says your name like it matters. Will's arrived when he was eight. Mike's took a lot longer.
Goth Will and punk Mike, sharing a cigarette neither of them wants behind a venue in 1989.
Single-parent AU: Will is raising a kid alone and Mike is the neighbor who keeps showing up with groceries nobody asked for and doesn't leave.
Beauty and the Beast, roughly: a monster in a locked house who is desperate to be seen as a person, and the boy who keeps coming back to the library anyway.
Superhero AU. Mike's powers are loud and public; Will's are quiet and dangerous. The city has picked a favorite and it's the wrong one.
Both of them are nineteen and broke, driving a car that shouldn't make it out of Indiana, with no plan past the next state line.
Zombie apocalypse. Will has been bitten, or thinks he has, and won't let Mike near him. Mike, being Mike, does not respect this at all.
Werewolf AU: the full moon has never scared Will. What scares him is who keeps waiting up in the woods for him to come back.
Modern-day, no monsters, no powers: they're just two boys at the same high school, and the hardest thing in the world is a hand held under a lunch table.
